related_questions.question: What is a good interest rate on a personal loan?

text_blocks.snippet: A "good" interest rate on a personal loan generally falls under 18%, and can be even better if it's below 10% for those with excellent credit. Rates are influenced by credit score, lender, and current market conditions.

list.title: Credit Score:
list.snippet: A higher credit score typically leads to lower interest rates.

list.title: Lender:
list.snippet: Different lenders (banks, credit unions, online lenders) offer varying rates.

list.title: Market Conditions:
list.snippet: Interest rates are influenced by the Federal Reserve's actions and the prime rate.

list.title: Loan Amount and Term:
list.snippet: Longer loan terms can mean higher overall interest paid, even with a lower monthly payment.
Some lenders offer rates as low as 5.99%.
Rates for those with excellent credit can be around 7.99%.
The average rate for a three-year loan from a credit union was 10.75% in March 2025 according to the National Credit Union Administration.
Some lenders have rates as high as 35.99%.

list.title: Shop around:
list.snippet: Compare offers from different lenders to find the best rate for your situation.

list.title: Consider fees:
list.snippet: Factor in origination fees or other charges, which can impact the overall cost of the loan.

list.title: Focus on the APR:
list.snippet: The annual percentage rate (APR) provides a clearer picture of the loan's total cost, including interest and fees.
